description_full: CI&T Inc., together with its subsidiaries, provides strategy, design, and software engineering services in North America, Europe, Latin America, Asia Pacific, and worldwide. It is also involved in the development of customizable software through the implementation of software solutions, including machine learning, artificial intelligence, data analytics, cloud migration, and mobility technologies. The company offers business and digital strategy, working closely with clients to understand strategic objectives, organizational constraints, and market dynamics; customer-centered experience and design, analyze customer and user journeys to design digital products, services, and platforms that improve efficiency, engagement, and satisfaction; and software engineering and platform delivery solutions, that designs, builds, modernizes, and operates digital platforms using agile, Lean, and DevOps practices. CI&T Inc. was founded in 1995 and is headquartered in Campinas, Brazil.

culture_narrative: Employs approximately 8K people. Revenue per employee of $55K ranks in the bottom quartile among Technology peers, improving at 29%/yr — growing workforce leverage. Each employee generates $7K of free cash flow annually.
financial_summary: CI&T Inc is a small-cap technology business with a $394M market cap on $448M of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +29% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are contracting by -2.1pp, the first warning that competitive pressure is eroding the franchise.
Returns on capital run at 10% against a 10% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, with gross margins sitting at 35%.

The business throws off $54M in free cash flow — roughly 12 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.23× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 1.1× net debt/EBITDA, and thin 1.9× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.
Shareholder yield of 2.2% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 2.1% of the shares.

sect: Its 13% operating margin runs 6pp above the Technology median (7%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
It earns less of the sector's profit than its revenue share would suggest (0.55x).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 530 companies in the universe; the top four hold 29% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a steep downtrend, down 31% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits near the bottom of its 52-week range, 47% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 53% and a beta of 1.11, it moves roughly with the market, though its beta has shifted (1y 0.14 vs 5y 1.26), so read it loosely.
Trading is thin (about $207K a day), below the $1.0M liquidity floor flagged; building a position would move the price.
In past sell-offs it fell 72% in the 2022 bear market.
val: The stock trades 72% below its DCF fair value of $10.94, a meaningful margin of safety.
The fair-value models corroborate one another (dispersion 4%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $7.66 to $15.97 (P10-P90).
On multiples it looks cheap against Technology peers: P/E 11.0 vs 26.7, EV/EBITDA 6.8 vs 16.4 and P/FCF 7.3 vs 25.4 (sector median).
Earnings yields are attractive: an FCF yield of 13.8% (above the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 11.7% (vs the 8% bar).
The 10 covering analysts target $5.62 on average, 82% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
The price implies 7.3% annual cash-flow growth, 20pp less than the model expects.
prof: ROIC of 10% falls short of the cost of capital of 10.0%, so growth at these returns destroys value; returns have been steady (CV 0.04).
It runs a 35% gross margin and converts 12% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality looks solid: a Piotroski score of 7/9 and cash conversion of 2.23x.
ROE of 9% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (1.9x equity multiplier).
hlth: Leverage is conservative at 1.1x net debt to EBITDA ($43.6M of cash against $126.7M of debt), and interest cover is thin at 1.9x.
Goodwill makes up 51% of assets, a soft asset exposed to impairment.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 29.2% over 3 years.
At current returns, reinvesting 52% of profits supports about 5.1% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
Analysts expect 22.7% long-term annual earnings growth.
own: Insiders own a modest 2.1%, and institutions hold 35%.
Insiders have only bought over the past year (14 purchases, net $128K bought).
It returns 2.2% a year to shareholders (2.2% in buybacks).
The share count has grown 2.1% a year over five years, diluting existing holders.
people: With about 8,152 employees, each generates about $55K of revenue, 0.1x the Technology median, and productivity has risen 29.2% a year.
That works out to $7K of free cash flow per employee.
